decisions.evidence: Read the full proof. The tower disjointness step is exact (a common point of T^{-i}W and T^{-j}W would put T^ix in W and T^{j-i}(T^ix) in W, contradicting that W has no positive return to E), each level has measure mu(W) by pullback invariance, and N mu(W) <= mu(X) forces mu(W)=0. Boundary cases E empty and mu(X)=0 are covered. Deps match the cited facts.

Read the full proof. A point of E with finitely many positive returns has a largest visit time q >= 0, so T^qx lies in W and x lies in N = union_m T^{-m}W, which is null by the tower lemma and countable subadditivity; conversely E cap N consists exactly of the exceptional points. The no-return case is the case q=0. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The basis exceptional sets are given by explicit formulas, so their countable union is null without any choice of covers; step 2.1 refines an arbitrary neighbourhood through an open V and a basis member B. The metric case's least-index recursion makes each admissible time set nonempty and yields strictly increasing n_j with d(T^{n_j}x,x)<1/j. Accepted.

Read the definition against its suppliers. The first-return time uses well-ordering of the naturals, the infinitely returning core is the set-limsup with mu(E setminus E_infinity)=0 by recurrence, and the induced map is a self-map of that core because the visits after r_E(x) are exactly the positive visits of T_E(x). The trace sigma-algebra on E_infinity is identified with measurable subsets of the core and mu_E is a probability. Explicitly choice-free.

Read the full proof. The level sets {r_E=n}=E cap T^{-n}E cap cap_{j<n}T^{-j}(X setminus E) are measurable with the empty intersection at n=1, the infinite level is the complement of their union, and measurability of r_E follows on the countable target. For T_E the identity T_E^{-1}B = union_n (E_infinity cap H_n cap T^{-n}B) is correct. Accepted.

Read the full proof and recomputed the identities R_{N+1}=T^{-1}R_N cap E^c, H_{N+1}=T^{-1}R_N cap E, T_E^{-1}B = disjoint union of H_n cap E_infinity, and the reverse inequality from applying the result to E_infinity setminus B with T_E^{-1}E_infinity=E_infinity. Neither invertibility nor ergodicity is used, matching the stated strength.

Read the full proof. U=union_n T^{-n}E_infinity is conull by sweep-out and strictly invariant; q(x) is the first entrance time into the core with measurable fibers. For an everywhere invariant finite real f on the core, F(x)=f(T^{q(x)}x) is measurable and T-invariant, including the cases x in the core (q(Tx)=r_E(x)-1), x in U setminus E_infinity and x outside U; ergodicity of T makes F constant a.e., so T_E is ergodic. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The identities mu(E cap {r_E>j}) = mu(C_j)-mu(C_{j+1}) come from pulling back C_j and splitting at E; the truncations min(r_E,N) telescope to 1-mu(C_N); sweep-out gives mu(C_N)->0 by continuity from above at total mass one; monotone convergence gives the value one including infinite return times on the null complement of E_infinity. The normalized form 1/mu(E) follows. Accepted.

Read the full proof and verified the finite identity int f = int_E sum_{j<N} f(T^jx)1_{r_E>j} + int f(T^Nx)1_{A_N} through the pullback step A_N cap E^c = C_{N+1} and A_{N+1}=T^{-1}C_{N+1}. The bounded case closes by the remainder bound M mu(A_N), truncation gives the general nonnegative case by monotone convergence, and the integrable case applies |f| first so no infinity is subtracted. Accepted.

Read the definition against its suppliers. The circle metric is verified (the integer minimum is attained, symmetry and the triangle inequality hold), rotations are isometries and doubling is 2-Lipschitz, the rational balls form a countable base and both Borel sigma-algebras agree, and lambda is a probability by endpoint nullness. The countable-choice boundary for the Lebesgue constructions is stated explicitly.

Read the full proof. The two-piece inverse image formula for a={alpha} is exact, the pieces are disjoint with measures adding to lambda(B) by translation invariance, and the generator test and completion clause apply under the declared countable choice. Invertibility with measurable inverse R_{-alpha} is proved by the same computation at -alpha. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The pigeonhole gives q with 0<q<=N and 0<d({q alpha},0)<1/N, and changing sign gives beta in (0,1/N) in the subgroup. Multiples of beta leave gaps of at most beta, so every circle point is within beta of the subgroup; the strengthened statement uses delta=min_{1<=q<=M}d({q alpha},0)>0 to force q>M. Every step is finite or least-index, so the choice-free claim holds.

Read the full proof. The rational case builds a strictly invariant Borel set of measure 1/2. In the irrational case, at density points a in A and c in A^c with r below 1/10 and below the cut distances, choosing m with d(R^m a,c)<r/10 makes S=R^mI cap J have measure at least 19r/10, while every point of S lies in J cap A or in R^mI setminus A, each of measure below r/5, so lambda(S)<2r/5: a contradiction. Completion case included.

Read the definition. The b-adic cells partition [0,1), on each cell D_b^n is b^n x minus the cell index, every branch is a bijection onto the circle with the displayed inverse, and the Lipschitz bound gives continuity. The identified doubling map is D_2, and no measure or choice assumption is used, as stated.

Read the full proof. The preimage of a half-open interval is the disjoint union of b half-open intervals of total length c-a, the generator test applies, and surjectivity and non-injectivity are explicit (y/b and the pair 0, 1/b). Countable choice enters only through the declared Lebesgue, dilation and completion suppliers. Accepted.

Read the full proof. For n>=r the cell I_{r,k} splits into b^{n-r} depth-n cells and each contributes a preimage interval of length b^{-(n+s)}, so lambda(I cap D_b^{-n}J) is exactly b^{-r-s} for every n>=r; the generating pi-system criterion gives Borel mixing and the symmetric-difference argument gives the completed case. Accepted.

Read the proof as the b=2 specialization: it correctly invokes the integer-base theorem, the fractional-part identification D=D_2, continuity, surjectivity and non-injectivity, and displays the two explicit branches with total length c-a. Accepted.

Read the full proof. Strict invariance gives (D^n)^{-1}A=A, hence A cap I_{n,k}=(A+k)/2^n and lambda(A cap I_{n,k})=2^{-n}lambda(A). At a density point the cell satisfies lambda(I_n setminus A)/h_n <= 2lambda((x-h_n,x+h_n) setminus A)/(2h_n)->0, while the same ratio equals 1-lambda(A) identically; hence lambda(A) is 0 or 1. Accepted.

Read the proof as the b=2 specialization of the integer-base mixing theorem, including the retained dyadic computation 2^{n-r}2^{-(n+s)}=2^{-r-s}=lambda(I)lambda(J) for n>=r and the depth-zero and empty-set cases. Accepted.

Read the definition. Finite unions of cylinders form an algebra, the G-atoms are disjoint, nonempty and partition Omega, and the content m2^{-|G|} is well defined because refining G to H splits each atom into 2^{|H|-|G|} atoms of equal total mass; finite additivity follows by common refinement. Total mass one, cylinder mass 2^{-|F|} and choice-freeness are verified.

Read the full proof. The metric is an ultrametric, a prefix cylinder is the ball of radius 2^{-(m-1)}, finite-coordinate cylinders are finite unions of prefixes, and cylinders are clopen. The compactness argument descends deterministically from a cover with no finite subcover, taking the zero child when it also lacks one and the one child otherwise, and produces x whose prefix cylinder is covered by a single member of the cover, a contradiction. ZF as claimed.

Read the full proof. For a disjoint countable family with union A in the algebra, the complements together with the A_n form an open cover, compactness reduces to finitely many A_n covering A, and disjointness makes every remaining term empty. Hence the content is countably additive on the algebra, with total mass one. Choice-free.

Read the full proof. Prefix cylinders form a countable base determining the Borel sigma-algebra, Caratheodory extension gives the Borel probability, uniqueness follows because two measures with the same cylinder masses agree on the algebra, and the completion is a complete probability. Countable choice is used exactly as declared. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The preimage of a cylinder is the cylinder on the shifted coordinate set with the same mass, continuity is immediate, and for cylinders C on F and H on G the intersection with sigma^{-n}H is a cylinder on the disjoint union F union (G+n) of mass p(C)p(H) once n is large. The completed case follows by null symmetric differences and strong mixing gives ergodicity. Accepted.

Read all steps. The algebra of polynomials in the distance functions to a countable dense set separates points; its uniform closure is a lattice by the cited Stone-Weierstrass-type lemma; the families A_x and G replace pointwise choice by compactness over finite subcovers, producing g in H with |g-f|<=eta; and rational-coefficient polynomials are uniformly dense with the delta/[r(1+M_i)] estimate. The AC_omega uses are exactly the declared dense subset, countable unions and lattice-lemma selections.

Read all seven steps. The 1-Lipschitz cutoffs t_U with compact support, rho(U)=sup Lambda over f prec U and mu* as the infimum over open supersets are well defined; the explicit partition phi_i=w_i min(2/delta,1/w) is a finite subordinate partition built from compactness; open-set subadditivity, Caratheodory measurability of open sets, the compact formula mu(F)=inf{Lambda(h):h>=1_F}, inner regularity on opens and the layer-cake equality Lambda(f)=int f dmu with error at most epsilon are each verified. Countable choice is spent only on the open supersets.

Read the full proof. The bisection rule is deterministic (left half first, then the least eligible index), the nested intervals have lengths 2M2^{-m}, the diagonal S_j construction gives n_r as the r-th member of S_r and hence strictly increasing indices, and the uniform Cauchy estimate transfers convergence from a countable dense family to all continuous functions. The limit functional meets the representation lemma, which supplies the regular probability. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The Cesaro measures integrate continuous functions as the displayed averages; the telescoping identity int(f circ T - f)dmu_N=(f(T^Nx)-f(x))/N vanishes in the limit; the pushforward nu(E)=mu(T^{-1}E) is a Borel probability with int f dnu=int f circ T dmu; and closed sets are determined by 1-h_m increasing to 1_{K setminus F} together with finite-measure pi-system uniqueness. Countable choice enters only through the subsequence lemma. Accepted.

Read the refutation. Doubling is non-injective, and the stronger argument shows no injective conull restriction exists: for each x in [0,1/2) one of x, x+1/2 lies in the complement N, so [0,1/2) is contained in N union (N-1/2), null by translation invariance, contradicting its measure 1/2. The definition clause about invariant conull restrictions is addressed explicitly. Accepted.

Read the refutation. The least-index recursion n_j exists by the strengthened density lemma and is unique; the translation overlap computation gives lambda(A cap R_alpha^{-n_j}A)=1/2-delta_j with delta_j->0, while strong mixing would force the limit 1/4. Irrationality supplies ergodicity. Accepted.

Read the refutation. Translation by one preserves Lebesgue measure with T^{-1}A=A-1, the total mass is infinite, E=[0,1) has measure one, and T^n x=x+n is at least one for n>=1, so no point returns at a positive time. Accepted.

Read the refutation. The dyadic rationals Q_2 are countable and null, contain 0 and omit 1/3 (three does not divide 2^n), and are strictly invariant: dyadic points stay dyadic, and from D(x)=k/2^n one gets 2x=k/2^n+ell with ell in {0,1}, so x is dyadic. This correctly separates strict invariance from the mod-null invariant-set criterion. Accepted.

Read the refutation. D(0)=0 gives the orbit {0}, and the ball of radius 1/8 about 1/2 is disjoint from it because d(0,1/2)=1/2; the ergodicity supplier is cited with its countable-choice assumption. Accepted.

Read the refutation. The atomic measure is invariant under D (the permutation 0, 1/3, 2/3 is checked through inverse-image masses), the eventual-zero set Z is strictly invariant of measure 1/2 so the system is not ergodic, and every everywhere invariant continuous function is constant because f(k/2^n)=f(0) and dyadic points q_n tend to x. Accepted.

Read the verification. For x=j/q+t with 0<=t<1/(2q) the rotation lands in the interval with index (j+p) mod q, that residue map is a permutation, and the half-open endpoint convention makes R^{-1}E=E exact. The q intervals are disjoint of total measure 1/2, so the rotation is not ergodic. Accepted.

Read the verification. The two branches give D^{-1}[0,1/2)=[0,1/4) union [1/2,3/4) of total measure 1/2, and the forward image of [0,1/2) is all of [0,1) of measure one, correctly contrasting inverse-image preservation with forward images. Endpoint images are computed explicitly. Accepted.

Read the verification. The three branch solutions give exactly [0,1/9) union [1/3,4/9) union [2/3,7/9), and I_{2,3a+c} maps affinely onto I_{1,c} with the half-open endpoints preserved, including the excluded right endpoint 1. No ternary expansion is chosen. Accepted.

Read the verification. The prescribed-coordinate counts give 1/2, 1/4 and 1/8, and sigma^{-3}[10] prescribes x_3=1, x_4=0, so the intersection with [01] is the cylinder on {0,1,3,4} of mass 1/16, equivalently the disjoint union [01010] union [01110]. Accepted.

Read the verification. D^{-1}[0,1/4)=[0,1/8) union [1/2,5/8) so the time-one return set is [0,1/8) of measure 1/8; the point 1/5 has return time four through the orbit 2/5,4/5,3/5,1/5; recurrence applies to the Borel set of measure 1/4. Accepted.

Read the verification. E=[0,1/2] has measure 1/2 with the endpoint null, the irrational rotation is ergodic, and Kac gives unnormalized mean one and normalized mean 1/lambda(E)=2. The closed-set convention is used consistently and no endpoint comparison is smuggled in. Accepted.
Read the counterexample. D^{-1}{0}={0,1/2} because 2x integral forces x in {0,1/2}; the symmetric difference with {0} is {1/2}, null, while the sets differ. Accepted.

Read the counterexample. delta_0 is invariant and ergodic, the atomic mixture is invariant with matching inverse-image masses, and the strictly invariant eventual-zero set has mass 1/2, so the mixture is not ergodic. The item correctly avoids the design note that wrongly called delta_0 non-ergodic. Accepted.

Read the counterexample. f(x)=e^{2 pi i x} has modulus one, satisfies f circ R_{1/2}=-f so its mean is zero, and (f circ R_alpha^n) conj(f)=e^{2 pi i n alpha}|f|^2, whose integral has modulus one for every n; the Cesaro average is identically one and cannot vanish. Ergodicity and the exact weak-mixing criterion are cited. Accepted.

Read the counterexample. The identity map preserves the probability but is not ergodic since E=[0,1/2] is strictly invariant of measure 1/2; r_E is identically one on E, so the unnormalized integral is 1/2 and the normalized mean is one, both differing from the ergodic conclusions one and two. Accepted.

Read all four steps. The interval integrals of h=1/(log 2 (1+x)) follow from the log derivative and the Riemann/Lebesgue bridge; the exact preimages G^{-1}[0,s]={0} union union_n[1/(n+s),1/n] telescope through log((1+1/n)/(1+1/(n+s))) to log(1+s)-log(1+s/(M+1))->log(1+s), matching mu([0,s]); the s=0 set is the enumerated null set {0} union {1/n:n>=2}; the pi-system generation, completion and independent inverse-branch density computation are correct. Accepted.

Read the whole A page against its 34 listed items in order. The narrative describes exactly the authored chain: no-return towers, finite-measure recurrence, topological recurrence, the induced system on the recurrent core with restricted measure, Kac return and excursion formulas, circle rotations and integer-base maps, the direct fair-coin cylinder construction, compact metric dynamics culminating in Krylov-Bogolyubov, and the five false-statement items. Page order is a valid prerequisite order, the choice statements match the items (AC_omega for the completed Lebesgue and fair-coin measures, the compact-probability route and the Gauss measure), and no claim stronger than the items is made.

Read the whole B page against its 11 examples and counterexamples. The prose matches the items: rational-rotation invariant sets, dyadic and ternary preimage computations, tabulated fair-coin cylinders, recurrence to [0,1/4), Kac mean return two for the half-circle, the mod-null versus strict invariance example, doubling ergodicity depending on the invariant measure, the non-weak-mixing exponential observable, the identity-map Kac failure, and the Gauss measure telescoping computation. No new mathematics is asserted and no item outside the manifest is referenced.

Read the full proof. E|Z|=2g(0), EZ=0 by symmetry with dominating majorant, EZ^2=1 by parts with boundary 2Rg(R)->0; phi_Z satisfies phi'=-t phi through finite-interval integration by parts and dominated convergence, so H(t)=e^{t^2/2}phi_Z(t) has zero derivative and equals one; the affine transform and the sigma=0 point mass are consistent. AC is used exactly as declared.

Read the full proof. The Taylor bounds give |r(u)|<=|u|^3/3 and |r(u)|<=4u^2 as well as |e^{iu}-1-iu|<=u^2; the dominated-convergence step uses the majorant X^2 min(|X|/(3n),4), valid for 0<|t|<=1/n, so the remainder is o(t^2) with only a finite second moment and no frequency subsequence. The 1-cos bound is included and sigma=0 is handled. Accepted.

Read the full proof. For |w|<=1/2 the exponential series gives |e^w-1-w|<=|w|^2; the finite product telescoping identity is applied with a_k=1+w_{n,k} and b_k=e^{w_{n,k}}, and the partial products are bounded by e^M, so the difference is at most e^M sum_k |w_{n,k}|^2 -> 0. Empty rows and M=0 are covered. Accepted.

Read the full proof. Standardizing by mean and standard deviation preserves independence and gives centered variance-one variables; the expansion gives n w_n -> -t^2/2 and hence the three hypotheses of the near-one product lemma; the product therefore tends to the standard normal transform, which is continuous at zero. The item correctly excludes sigma=0 because the normalization divides by sigma. Accepted.

Read the full proof. AC gives a choice function on the image family of any countable family, which yields countable choice, and AC gives a fixed fiber-choice function s(x)=c(R[x]) for a serial relation, whose recursion from the prescribed a yields the dependent-choice sequence. The lemma asserts only these implications and uses exactly two fixed-family selections. Accepted.

Read the full proof. AC supplies DC and countable choice, the Bernoulli law has independent copies, the partial sums have law Bin(n,p), and p(1-p)>0 for 0<p<1, so the iid CLT gives the standardized limit; equality of laws transfers it to the prescribed B_n without needing a coupling. Accepted.

Read the definition against the cited independence and expectation items. Row-wise factorization is stated for all Borel boxes with the subfamily reduction supplied by taking unused boxes to be the line, rows may live on different probability spaces, and single-entry rows, zero entries and the exclusion of empty rows are explicit. No choice or existence assumption is made. Accepted.

Read the definition. v_{n,k}, s_n and L_n are well defined with finite nonnegative terms, 0<=L_n(epsilon)<=1, and the normalized and unnormalized Lindeberg quantities are shown to be equal using |Y|>epsilon iff |X|>epsilon s_n and scalar homogeneity; the strict cutoff and the zero-variance exclusion are explicit. Choice-free. Accepted.

Read the full proof. Splitting E X^2 at the cutoff gives max_k Var(X_{n,k})<=epsilon^2+L_n(epsilon), and choosing epsilon<sqrt(eta/2) with n large proves max_k Var -> 0. Zero entries and the cutoff convention are handled, and independence is not used. Accepted.

Read the full proof. Centering gives |w_{n,k}|<=t^2 v_{n,k}, so sum|w|<=t^2, max|w|->0 and sum|w|^2<=t^4 max_k v_{n,k}->0; the two-region estimate |sum_k E r(tY_{n,k})|<=|t|^3 epsilon/3+4t^2 L_n(epsilon) gives sum w->-t^2/2 after taking limsup and then epsilon->0; the near-one product lemma and Levy then give the limit. Accepted.

Read the full proof. The bounds on w give the product lemma hypotheses, so exp(sum w_{n,k})->e^{-t^2/2} from the assumed limit and the forward continuity theorem. With d_t(x)=t^2x^2/2-(1-cos(tx)) one has Re sum w=-t^2/2+D_n(t) and |exp(sum w)|=e^{-t^2/2+D_n(t)}, so D_n(t)->0; at the single frequency t=4/epsilon, d_t>=t^2x^2/4 on |x|>epsilon yields the Lindeberg tail bound. No converse or logarithm is used. Accepted.

Read the full proof. On |X|>epsilon s_n one has X^2<=|X|^{2+delta}/(epsilon s_n)^delta, so L_n(epsilon)<=epsilon^{-delta}s_n^{-(2+delta)}sum_k E|X_{n,k}|^{2+delta}->0 for each fixed epsilon; Lindeberg and the sufficiency theorem give the limit. delta>0 is fixed and delta=0 is excluded with the stated reason. Accepted.

Read the definition against its suppliers. The realization m+Sigma^{1/2}Z has projections with the required scalar normal laws, hence mean m and covariance Sigma; singular Sigma and Sigma=0 are covered by the point mass, and uniqueness is correctly deferred to the following characteristic-function lemma. AC is spent in the standard-normal construction, the independent-copy realization and the scalar uniqueness supplier.

Read the full proof. Projection laws give the transform exp(it dot m - t^T Sigma t/2), including degenerate directions t^T Sigma t=0 where the law is the point mass at t dot m; uniqueness follows from scalar uniqueness on projections plus Cramer-Wold. No determinant or inverse is used, so singular Sigma is covered. Accepted.

Read the full proof. Projections are iid centered with variance u^T Sigma u; for positive variance the scalar CLT and continuous scaling give the projection limit, and for zero variance E Y_k^2=0 forces Y_k=0 almost surely, with finitely many exceptional sets per row, giving the exact degenerate law. Cramer-Wold then gives the vector limit and no common null set is claimed. Accepted.

Read the remark. It asserts only distributional convergence for the cited theorems, correctly distinguishes it from convergence in probability and almost sure convergence, notes that the constant-limit special case applies to degenerate Gaussians, and disclaims rates. No statement beyond the cited items is made. Accepted.

Read the verification and recomputed the illustration. The endpoints form a null boundary set, so the continuity-set implication of the portmanteau theorem applies; for n=100, p=1/2 the raw endpoints -1,1 give about 0.68268949 and the half-unit endpoints 89/2,111/2 standardize to -1.1,1.1 giving about 0.72866788. The item correctly disclaims any finite-n error bound. Accepted.

Read the verification. The density gives a probability with EU=1/2, EU^2=1/3 and Var=1/12 by the primitive computation, and sqrt(12/n)=1/sqrt(n/12) converts the CLT into the displayed form; the copy construction is invoked only if realization is needed, with AC supplying DC and countable choice. Accepted.

Read the verification. E|X_{n,k}|^3=k^3, s_n^2>=n^3/8 because at least n/2 indices satisfy k>=n/2, and sum k^3<=n^4, so s_n^{-3}sum_k E|X_{n,k}|^3<=8^{3/2}/sqrt n -> 0 and delta=1 applies; distinct laws follow from disjoint supports. Accepted.

Read the verification. p_{n,k}=k/(2n+2) lies in (0,1/2), the centered Bernoulli variances are p(1-p), sum_k k=n(n+1)/2 gives s_n^2>=n/8, every entry has modulus below one so for fixed epsilon the tail event is eventually empty and Lindeberg holds exactly, and distinct p give distinct laws. Accepted.

Read the verification. The covariance sigma^2[[1,1],[1,1]] is rank one with eigenvalues 2sigma^2 and 0, the multivariate CLT applies to the iid vectors (Y_k,Y_k), and the limit is identified with the law of (Z,Z) by comparing projections, with the (1,-1) direction vanishing. Accepted.

Read all four steps. The Laplace transform 1/(1+t^2) is computed from explicit primitives; integrability and density inversion give the Cauchy density c; the inversion identity gives int e^{iux}c(x)dx=e^{-|u|}; the second moment diverges by int_1^R x^2 c >= (R-1)/(2pi); and the normalized-sum transforms e^{-sqrt n|t|} converge pointwise to a function discontinuous at zero, so the forward continuity theorem and continuity of characteristic functions exclude any weak limit. Accepted.

Read the counterexample. The array with X_{n,1}=Z and X_{n,k}=0 is centered and row-wise independent, has total variance one and row sums exactly N(0,1), and maximum summand variance one; the Lindeberg quantity equals E[Z^2 1_{|Z|>epsilon}], which is strictly positive by the lower bound (epsilon+1)^2 e^{-(epsilon+2)^2/2}/sqrt(2 pi) on the length-one interval [epsilon+1,epsilon+2]. Accepted.
